reviews.text:
Bug Report: Incorrect Juz Number Displayed in Quran Mushaf

Title: Incorrect Juz Number / Missing Juz 5 & Juz 6 Mapping in Quran Mushaf

Description:

I found a serious issue with the Juz classification displayed in the Quran Mushaf section of the Noor app.

The app is displaying incorrect Juz numbers for several Quran verses. Based on the standard Juz division of the Quran, the following verses are incorrectly labelled:

* An-Nisaa’ 4:114 — App displays Juz 4 ❌ — Correct: Juz 5 ✅
* An-Nisaa’ 4:148 — App displays Juz 4 ❌ — Correct: Juz 6 ✅
* An-Nisaa’ 4:171 — App displays Juz 4 ❌ — Correct: Juz 6 ✅
* An-Nisaa’ 4:176 — App displays Juz 4 ❌ — Correct: Juz 6 ✅
* Al-A’raaf 7:164 — App displays Juz 8 ❌ — Correct: Juz 9 ✅
* Yaseen 36:28 — App displays Juz 22 ❌ — Correct: Juz 23 ✅

This does not appear to be an isolated typo.

The screenshots indicate that Juz 5 is being skipped, while verses belonging to Juz 6 are still being labelled as Juz 4. There are also incorrect Juz labels in later parts of the Quran, such as Al-A’raaf and Yaseen.

This suggests that there may be an issue with the Juz mapping/indexing data used by the Quran Mushaf feature.

Expected behaviour:
The app should display the correct Juz number according to the standard Quran Juz division for every verse.

Actual behaviour:
Several verses are assigned to the wrong Juz, as demonstrated in the attached screenshots.

Platform: iOS / iPhone
Feature: Quran → Mushaf
Issue: Incorrect Juz classification/mapping

Please in

reviews.title: Prayer times
reviews.text:
I would like to report a serious concern regarding the prayer times displayed in the Noor app.

The prayer times in the app do not consistently match the official timings provided by JAKIM. This issue was first noticed during the last 10 nights of Ramadan. It was briefly resolved, but the discrepancy has now reappeared.

This raises an important question: which source is Noor actually following for its prayer times? Is it based on JAKIM, or another reference? More importantly, is there an active monitoring or verification process by the developers to ensure accuracy?

Prayer times are extremely sensitive and cannot be treated lightly. Inaccurate timings can directly affect users’ religious obligations. I strongly urge the development team to investigate this issue thoroughly and ensure that the app aligns with official and reliable sources such as JAKIM.

Thank you.

reviews.title: Prayer time not accurate at all even though the location is correct and has been refreshed
reviews.text:
I have been a loyal TheNoor user for quite some time and have always appreciated the app and its features. However, lately I’ve noticed that the prayer times shown in the app are not accurate compared to the official local prayer schedule. This is quite concerning because many users rely on the app for correct prayer timings.  

I hope the team can look into this issue and update or fix the prayer time calculations as soon as possible. Thank you for your efforts in maintaining the app, and I hope it continues to improve.

reviews.title: Backward Update
reviews.text:
I feel like the recent update is a step backwards. Some good features that were previously available are no longer there. Like many others have mentioned, the auto-scroll feature while reading the Quran is gone, which was very helpful.

The new Infaq Tree also feels like a downgrade compared to the previous tracker, which was much clearer and more useful.

Another disappointing change is the shift of features to Pro. For a spiritual app that was originally created to help people with their faith and good deeds, locking useful features behind a paid subscription feels against that original purpose. It starts to feel less about helping the community and more about monetisation.

I understand that apps need funding to continue operating, but removing helpful features and placing them behind a paywall is discouraging.

Unfortunately, this update has made the experience worse for me. If things continue this way, the app might lose a user here. Really disappointed with the direction of this update.

reviews.title: Not responsive
reviews.text: After the recent upgrade, the Noor App looks nicer with its new interface, but it has become less responsive. When I try to search for a surah name, nothing shows up, even though this worked in the previous version. Also, when I try to change the language, the app doesn’t respond to the option I selected. Hopefully these issues can be fixed in the next update.

reviews.title: Ayat selection and audio run not as good as before
reviews.text: I used to read the Quran while following the reciter’s voice in this app, and it worked very well before. However, after the recent update, the audio no longer stops at the selected ayah. Even when I tap the play button on a specific ayah, it starts reciting from a different ayah instead. It’s quite confusing and difficult to follow now. I really wish it could be as simple and user-friendly as it was before.

reviews.title: 2026 Updated Version | Didn’t work well
reviews.text:
I used to love the previous version where the app funtioned seamlessly. With the new update, the Quran features does not work well. 

1. It does not open the surah where you bookmarked them. 

2. The recitation does not play at the exact ayat where you are currently navigating. 

3. Good that the app now has the “Last Read” feature. However when you click it, it will only brings you to Al-Faatihah

4. The translation can’t change to another language, although you have done so at the settings. 

I hope this can be fixed soon. The Noor app really helps me with my Quran reading. Especially now, during Ramadhan. I felt a bit frustrated with all these current issues happening with the app.
